summary: Wrote a 6-phase, 9-hour plan covering all three lean-challenge-snapshot.sh defects, re-deriving every site and figure against the source store rather than trusting the dispatch or report. Two research conclusions were corrected: lean/manifest.json enumerates challenge fixtures individually and omits plan_goals_preamble.md, so a redeploy alone cannot fix the deployed R8 failure (manifest.json added to scope, and every new fixture must be registered); and the report's concrete Goals-harvest rule would have turned fixtures R1 and R7 red, so the plan adopts an identifier-leading-bullet rule with explicit fixture migration. The plan also decouples chunk-boundary detection from name harvesting and body forcing, which a naive alternation widening would conflate into newly requiring every abbrev to be a Goal.

artifacts.summary: 6-phase serial plan: commit landed R6/R7/R8 work plus manifest fixture registration; one shared Unicode-aware identifier definition across all four Python sites; decoupled declaration-boundary widening; identifier-leading Goals rule with a cross-repo plan-format decision gate; opt-in --dry-run compile step; full gate set and deployed-tree parity.
